questions.enonce_markdown: An appropriate strategy to encourage industrialization in Cameroon is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Industrialization is encouraged by making it cheaper and more profitable to set up factories. A tax holiday (a period during which a new firm pays no or reduced company tax) lowers the start-up cost and attracts investors, so it is a standard incentive. Employing foreign labour does not build local industry; closing training centres reduces the supply of skilled workers; discouraging agricultural exports removes the foreign exchange and raw-material base that industry needs.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Grant tax holidays to new industries.
Employ foreign labour force in the industry.
Close down training centres to lay emphasis on production.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the government sets the price of a good below equilibrium, it will lead to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A price fixed below the equilibrium price is a maximum (ceiling) price. At that low price consumers want to buy more than producers are willing to supply, so quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied: there is excess demand (a shortage). Excess supply arises when the price is set ABOVE equilibrium (a minimum price). The price itself does not shift the demand or supply curves, it only moves along them (a change in quantity demanded and quantity supplied).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A gradual fall in the value of fixed assets over time is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Machines, buildings and vehicles lose value through wear and tear and obsolescence as they are used. This gradual loss of value of fixed capital is called capital depreciation (capital consumption). Capital formation is the addition of new capital goods; replacement is buying new assets to take the place of worn-out ones; maintenance is the upkeep of existing assets.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The quality of money which ensures that all transactions are made possible in an economy is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
For money to make every transaction possible, everybody must be ready to take it in payment for goods, services and debts. This quality is general acceptability. Divisibility allows small and large payments, portability makes money easy to carry, and durability means it lasts, but none of these guarantees that a seller will accept it.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The basic economic question concerned with the distribution of goods and services is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Every economy must answer three basic questions: WHAT to produce (which goods and in what quantity), HOW to produce (which methods and combination of factors) and FOR WHOM to produce (how the output is shared among the members of society, that is its distribution). The question about distribution is therefore "for whom to produce".

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A government policy achieved by setting minimum and maximum prices is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Setting a minimum price (a floor) or a maximum price (a ceiling) is a direct control over the market, as are rationing and licensing. In the Cameroon O Level syllabus such direct controls are called physical policy (physical or direct controls). Monetary policy works through the money supply and interest rates, fiscal policy through taxation and government spending, and regional policy aims at spreading development between regions.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A likely economic problem that will result when outputs of some firms become the inputs of others in national income accounting:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The output of one firm (for example cocoa beans) is the input of another (a chocolate factory). If the value of both the intermediate good and the final good is added to national income, the same value is counted more than once. This is double counting, which is avoided by counting only final goods or by adding value added at each stage. Stock appreciation and depreciation concern changes in the value of stocks, and the black economy concerns unrecorded activities.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A complete shift of the demand curve to the right is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A movement along a given demand curve, caused by a change in the price of the good itself, is a change in quantity demanded. A shift of the WHOLE curve is caused by other factors (income, tastes, prices of related goods, population), and a shift to the right means that more is demanded at every price: an increase in demand. Option B (a change in demand) is true of a shift in either direction, but only D says that the shift is to the right.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank customer, Mary, has 70,000FCFA in her current account at BICEC and she is allowed to withdraw 120,000FCFA. Determine the amount of overdraft given to her.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An overdraft is the amount withdrawn in excess of the balance on the current account.

Overdraft = amount withdrawn - balance = 120,000 - 70,000 = **50,000 FCFA**.

The first 70,000 FCFA is her own money; only the extra 50,000 FCFA is lent by the bank. Option D (190,000) wrongly adds the two amounts.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How much will a Cameroon businessman require to buy a car in FCFA, given that the said car cost 1000 pounds and where 1 pound = 600FCFA?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convert the price from pounds to FCFA by multiplying by the exchange rate.

Price in FCFA = 1,000 pounds × 600 FCFA per pound = **600,000 FCFA**.

Options A, C and D come from misplacing zeros.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Roads, national defence and street lights are good examples of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Public goods are provided by the government for the whole community because they are non-excludable (nobody can be prevented from using them) and non-rival (one person's use does not reduce another's). Roads, national defence and street lights fit this description. Consumer goods are bought by households for their own use, merit goods (such as education) are under-consumed if left to the market, and free goods (such as air) have no opportunity cost.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: At what price will a consumer be able to buy 8 apples, given that the demand function is P = 240 - 5Q, where P is price in FCFA and Q is the quantity of apples?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute Q = 8 into the demand function.

P = 240 - 5Q = 240 - 5 × 8 = 240 - 40 = **200 FCFA**.

Option A (232) comes from subtracting 8 instead of 5 × 8, and B (280) from adding 40.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The theory which has a pessimistic view on the rapid population growth was proposed by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Thomas Malthus argued that population tends to grow faster (geometrically) than food supply (arithmetically), so rapid population growth leads to famine, disease and war unless it is checked: a pessimistic view. Esther Boserup took the opposite, optimistic view that population pressure pushes farmers to invent new methods and increase food output. Adam Smith and John Stuart Mill are not the authors of this theory.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many denominations of paper money exist in the currency used in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon uses the CFA franc of the CEMAC zone. Its paper notes are of 500, 1,000, 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 FCFA, that is **5 denominations** (coins are counted separately).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The omissions made when calculating national income are represented by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Because of mistakes, unrecorded transactions and timing differences, the accounts never balance perfectly. The correcting figure inserted in the accounts to make them balance and to represent what was left out or wrongly recorded is called "errors and omissions". Double counting is the opposite problem (counting a value more than once), and "balancing items" and "residual errors" are not the standard term used in the syllabus.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is a characteristic of development:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A developed economy is marked by high real income per head (real GDP per capita), long life expectancy, low infant mortality and a large number of consumer durables per head. Options A, B and C are all signs of underdevelopment. Only D describes a characteristic of development.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below are examples of some business organisations.

i) Sole proprietorship
ii) Partnership
iii) Joint stock company
iv) National/public corporations.

Identify two organisations from the list above which are unincorporated:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An unincorporated business has no separate legal personality: the owners and the business are the same in law, and the owners are personally liable for its debts. Sole proprietorship (i) and partnership (ii) are unincorporated. A joint stock company (iii) and a public corporation (iv) are incorporated, with their own legal personality. The pair is therefore i and ii.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A debt contracted for the fight against malaria is a good example of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Public debts are classified by purpose into productive debt (used to finance projects that earn revenue and so repay themselves, such as a power station or a road) and unproductive debt (used for purposes that bring in no direct revenue, such as war, relief of famine or the fight against an epidemic like malaria). A loan to fight malaria produces no income with which to repay it, so it is an unproductive debt. External and internal debt classify debt by the origin of the lender, not by what the money is used for.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When government decides to use price control to as measure to curb inflation, a category of inflation is produced known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the government fixes maximum prices, the rise in prices is held back by law although demand is still too high. The inflation is hidden or held in check rather than eliminated: it is suppressed (repressed) inflation, and it shows itself in shortages, queues and black markets. Creeping and galloping inflation describe the SPEED of price rises.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The ability of labour to increase output and quality of work within a short period of time is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Efficiency (productivity) of labour measures how much and how well a worker produces in a given time. Supply of labour is the number of workers or hours offered, mobility of labour is the ease of moving between jobs or places, and demand for labour is the number of workers firms want to employ.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A market situation in which there is only one buyer of a given commodity is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A market with a single buyer is a monopsony (for example one cocoa-buying company purchasing from many farmers). Monopoly is a single SELLER, and duopoly is two sellers. The word "oligosony" as printed is a misspelling of oligopsony (a few buyers), which does not describe a single buyer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The formula: value of visible exports, less value of visible imports, is used to calculate:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Visible items are physical goods. Value of visible exports - value of visible imports = balance of trade (trade in goods). The current account balance also includes invisibles (services, income, transfers), and the invisible balance is invisible exports less invisible imports.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "A situation where producers produce, taking into consideration what consumers want" is generally referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a market economy consumers, by spending their money, decide what is produced and producers follow their wishes. This is consumer sovereignty. Producer sovereignty is the opposite situation, where firms decide what to produce and persuade consumers to buy it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The exchange of goods and services between Cameroon and Japan can better be described as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade between exactly two countries is bilateral trade. International trade is the general word for trade between any countries, and multilateral trade involves several countries. Because only Cameroon and Japan are named, the more precise description is bilateral trade.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the bank operates on a cash rate of 10%, and receive an initial deposit of 100 million FCFA, it will create maximum deposit equal to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The credit (deposit) multiplier is 1 / cash ratio.

Multiplier = 1 / 0.10 = 10.

Maximum total deposits = initial deposit × multiplier = 100 million × 10 = **1,000 million FCFA = 1,000,000,000 FCFA**.

Option D is only the initial deposit, and C (90 million) is neither the total deposits nor the credit created (900 million).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When national income increases such that quality of life improves in an economy, we refer to it as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth is only an increase in real national income or output. When that increase also improves the quality of life of the people (health, education, living conditions, income distribution), we speak of economic development. Actual growth and potential growth are two kinds of growth and say nothing about quality of life.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The concentration of firms belonging to a particular industry in one region is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When many firms of the same industry are found together in one area (for example the cocoa-processing or timber firms of one town), we speak of the localisation of an industry. Industrialisation is the general development of industries in an economy, and "location of industry" is the choice of where a single firm sets up.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram below and answer question 28.

![fig-1](gce-ol-economics-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

What is the population size, which is considered to be optimum?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The optimum population is the population size at which output per head (average product) is at its maximum. The curve AP on the diagram shows the average product of labour. It rises from A (2,000 million tons at 1 million people), reaches its highest point at B (3,000 million tons) when the labour force is **2 million**, then falls (2,000 at 3 million and 1,000 at 4 million). The optimum population is therefore 2 million people.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Direct taxes meet the criteria of a good tax system for the reason that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A direct tax (income tax, company tax) is paid by the same person on whom it is levied, so the impact (who pays the tax first) and the incidence (who finally bears it) are the same and are easy to determine. This certainty is one of the criteria of a good tax. A is a weakness (avoidance), C describes indirect taxes on harmful goods such as tobacco, and B is not a general feature of direct taxes.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It discourages consumption of harmful goods
It is easy to determine tax incidence and impact

questions.enonce_markdown: The practice of division of labour is limited by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Adam Smith explained that the division of labour is limited by the extent of the market: if the market is small, demand is too low to justify specialised workers and large-scale production. Monotony and loss of craftsmanship are DISADVANTAGES of the division of labour, not limits on how far it can be applied.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 31 is based on the diagram below.

![fig-2](gce-ol-economics-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

What is the coefficient of price elasticity of demand?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The demand curve is a horizontal line at price P. At that single price consumers are ready to buy any quantity, and a very small rise in price would reduce the quantity demanded to zero. The percentage change in quantity demanded for a given percentage change in price is infinitely large, so demand is perfectly elastic: **PED = ∞**. A vertical demand curve would give PED = 0.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following restrictive trade instruments generate revenue to the state:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A tariff is a tax on imports collected by the customs, so it brings revenue to the state. An embargo is a ban on trade with a country, a quota is a physical limit on the quantity imported, and a subsidy is money PAID by the state (it costs revenue rather than generating it).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is a benefit of a small holder from the main plantation:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A small holder is an independent farmer who grows the same crop as the large plantation (for example oil palm or rubber) on his own land. The main plantation (the nucleus estate) typically supports small holders by supplying improved seeds and seedlings and technical advice, and by buying their output. Free houses go to the plantation's own workers, and free loans and free chemicals are not normally given at no cost.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Receive free chemical for their crops

questions.enonce_markdown: A market situation where there is excess demand, such that the supplier takes advantage to impose a price higher than the normal is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When demand is greater than supply, sellers are in a strong position and can charge more than the normal price: this is a sellers' market. A buyers' market is the opposite (supply greater than demand, so buyers dictate the price). A black market is an ILLEGAL market where goods are sold above the legal maximum price, and a monopoly market is defined by a single seller, not by excess demand.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is a direct form of state intervention in an economy:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Direct intervention means that the state controls the market itself through orders and rules: price control, rationing, licences and quotas. Taxes, subsidies and control of the money supply are INDIRECT forms, because they work by changing incentives or the amount of money, and leave firms and consumers free to decide.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Imposition of direct and indirect taxes

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following will reduce the supply of labour in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The supply of labour is the number of people (and hours) available for work. Extending the school leaving age keeps young people in school for longer, so fewer enter the labour force: supply falls. Raising the retirement age keeps older workers working, higher overtime pay makes workers offer more hours, and facilitating immigration adds workers, so all three increase the supply of labour.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Increase the pay for over time

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following will be the economic effect of increasing direct taxes in an economy:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Higher direct taxes (income tax and company tax) reduce households' disposable income and firms' retained profits. Consumption and investment therefore fall, so total demand falls, which tends to reduce output and employment and to ease inflation. Among the options, the effect that follows directly is a reduction in investment. A, B and D describe the opposite results.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A business organisation which operates with an objective "not for profit":
questions.corrige_markdown:
A co-operative society is owned by its members who join to help one another (for example farmers selling their cocoa together), and its main aim is service to members rather than profit maximisation. Sole traders, partnerships and public limited companies are all run for profit.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study this table that shows the different levels of satisfaction attained by a consumer of Good A and answer the question that follows:

| Units of consumption of Good A | Marginal utility (utils) | Total utility (utils) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100 | - |
| 2 | 60 | 160 |
| 3 | - | 200 |
| 4 | 10 | - |
| 5 | 00 | 210 |

What is the utility for this consumer, when he consumes one unit of Good A?
questions.corrige_markdown:
For the first unit consumed, the total utility equals the marginal utility, because there is no unit before it: TU(1) = MU(1) = **100 utils**.

The rest of the table is consistent with this: TU(2) = 100 + 60 = 160, MU(3) = 200 - 160 = 40, MU(4) = 10 so TU(4) = 210, and MU(5) = 0 so TU(5) = 210. Options B (160 = utility of two units), C (60 = marginal utility of the second unit) and D (40 = marginal utility of the third unit) are other cells of the table.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A market structure where firms practice product differentiation but there is freedom of entry and exit is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Monopolistic competition has many firms selling differentiated (similar but not identical) products, with free entry and exit. Perfect competition has identical products, monopoly has barriers to entry and a single seller, and oligopoly has a few large firms and barriers to entry.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Suppose the total cost of a company is 250,000 FCFA, total variable cost is 100,000 FCFA and output is 20 units, what is the total fixed cost?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total cost = total fixed cost + total variable cost, so

TFC = TC - TVC = 250,000 - 100,000 = **150,000 FCFA**.

The output of 20 units is not needed. Option D (350,000) wrongly adds TC and TVC.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A balance of payment deficit can be corrected in the short run by:

*Options as printed:* A) Increasing foreign reserves.   B) Devaluing a country's currency.   C) Selling investments abroad.   D) Reducing expenditure on imports.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A deficit means that payments to the rest of the world exceed receipts. Increasing foreign reserves (A) is the result of a surplus, not a cure for a deficit. Reducing expenditure on imports (D), by import restrictions or lower domestic demand, acts directly and quickly on the debit side of the account. Devaluation (B) works only after a delay (the J-curve effect), and a member of the CFA franc zone cannot devalue on its own. Selling investments abroad (C) finances the deficit by a capital inflow but does not remove its cause.

**Intended answer: D (Reducing expenditure on imports).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The cost of production which does not change as output changes in the short run is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the short run some factors (buildings, machines) cannot be changed, so the cost of them stays the same whatever the level of output: this is fixed cost. Variable cost, total cost and average cost all change when output changes.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Company AWZ decides to raise capital through the sale of shares as follows:

100 preference shares of 5% at 500frs each,
50 debentures of 5% at 1000frs each,
300 ordinary shares at 500frs each.

What is the value of capital raised by the sale of the most risky share?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ordinary shares are the most risky: their dividend is not fixed and is paid only after preference shareholders, and in liquidation they are paid last. Debentures are loans, not shares.

Capital raised by ordinary shares = 300 × 500 = **150,000 FCFA**.

For comparison, the 100 preference shares raise 100 × 500 = 50,000 FCFA (option A) and the debentures raise 50 × 1,000 = 50,000 FCFA; the whole issue raises 250,000 FCFA.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Assume the GDP for country Z is 450 billion FCFA and the GNP is 550 billion FCFA. What is the value of Net property Income Received from Abroad (NPIRA)?
questions.corrige_markdown:
GNP = GDP + net property income received from abroad, so

NPIRA = GNP - GDP = 550 - 450 = **100 billion FCFA**.

Option A adds the two figures.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mr. Tarh in a sunny day gets 50 utils in consuming a bottle of coke. When he settles for the second bottle, his total satisfaction rose to 90 utils. An attempt to consume the third bottle, his marginal utility fell to 30 utils. What is his total utility for consuming the third bottle?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total utility after the second bottle = 90 utils. The third bottle adds a marginal utility of 30 utils, so

TU(3) = TU(2) + MU(3) = 90 + 30 = **120 utils**.

Option C (170) wrongly adds 50 + 90 + 30. Option A (60) subtracts instead of adding.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which other name is given to "maximum price" used by the government to protect consumers?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A maximum price is the highest price that sellers are legally allowed to charge. It is also called a ceiling price, and it protects consumers from high prices. A floor price is a MINIMUM price, which protects producers.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Population of country Y is 30 million people. 40% is made up of the labour force, while 30% is made up of the young. Determine the dependency ratio of this population:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dependants are the young and the old; the working population is the labour force.

Young = 30%, working = 40%, so old = 100 - 40 - 30 = 30%.

Dependency ratio = (young + old) / working population × 100 = (30 + 30) / 40 × 100 = **150%**.

Option B (75%) is 30 / 40 × 100, which leaves out the old and counts only the young.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A government decides to borrow from its partners as follows:

Banks within the country 10 million FCFA
Corporate sector at home 20 million FCFA
Private individuals at home 5 million FCFA
Foreign Banks 40 million FCFA
Foreigners 25 million FCFA

What is the value of the internal debt?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Internal debt is owed to lenders inside the country; external debt is owed to foreign lenders.

Internal debt = 10 + 20 + 5 = **35 million FCFA**.

External debt = 40 + 25 = 65 million FCFA (option D), and the total debt is 100 million FCFA (option C).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the objectives of a central bank is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The central bank is not run to make profit. Its objectives include regulating the money supply and credit, maintaining the stability of prices and of the currency, and acting as banker to the government and to commercial banks. Profitability, liquidity and security are the objectives of COMMERCIAL banks, which must balance them.

**Answer: C.**
